The energy transition is about more than climate - it is about sustainable jobs, sovereignty, and inclusive economic growth. We need to refocus on human development at the center of energy.

Clean #energy now employs 35 million people worldwide, yet women represent only 32% of that workforce. Global investment has surpassed USD 2 trillion, outpacing fossil fuels—but translating this momentum into affordable, reliable, and inclusive energy remains the real challenge.

Smarter, decentralized systems can shift this balance. #Digital tools, #AI, and data-driven management can optimize demand, reduce losses, and improve reliability—helping every unit of energy power growth and resilience. Smarter grids alone could cut 1 gigaton of CO₂ annually and lower peak loads by 8–12% by 2050, while digitally enabled efficiency in public buildings can reduce energy use by up to 50%.

Yet energy and digital transitions are advancing faster than the systems that govern them and mitigate their risks. The priority now is pairing governance with institutional capacity and national innovation systems to make energy systems fairer, smarter, and more resilient.

This week in Skopje, I am pushing to advance these priorities during the 14th International Forum on Energy for Sustainable Development, focusing on scaling up action toward aligning innovation, governance, and human development for a just energy future.
